integration_patterns.title: Direct library integration
integration_patterns.choose_when: The project already exposes reusable domain or application APIs that can be called without starting its existing user interface.
integration_patterns.avoid_when: The reusable API is unstable, unsafe to call from a GUI process, or tied to a different event loop without an adapter.
required_evidence: Public entry points and ownership rules

integration_patterns.title: Service client
integration_patterns.choose_when: The project already exposes a local or remote HTTP, RPC, socket, or message-based service contract.
integration_patterns.avoid_when: The service contract is an internal implementation detail or the GUI must work fully offline without the service.

integration_patterns.title: Structured child process
integration_patterns.choose_when: The project has a stable command-line entry point but no safe in-process library boundary.
integration_patterns.avoid_when: The only output is human-oriented terminal control sequences or the process cannot report structured progress and errors.
required_evidence: Stable arguments or a JSON-lines protocol

integration_patterns.title: Native project extension
integration_patterns.choose_when: The host project has a documented plugin, frontend, or module extension point that can own a GUI surface.
integration_patterns.avoid_when: Using the extension point would require private host APIs or couple the GUI to an unstable ABI.

integration_patterns.title: Extract a reusable core
integration_patterns.choose_when: Business behavior is coupled to an existing UI entry point but can be separated with a narrow, test-preserving refactor.
integration_patterns.avoid_when: The requested GUI is too small to justify a broad refactor or the extraction would change established behavior without adequate tests.
required_evidence: A narrow interface independent of UI widgets
Both old and new frontends consume the same core

integration_patterns.title: Greenfield application
integration_patterns.choose_when: No reusable application exists yet, or the request is explicitly for a new standalone GUI product.
integration_patterns.avoid_when: An existing supported interface can satisfy the requirement with less duplication and lower maintenance cost.

application_patterns.title: Library frontend
signals: The repository primarily exposes a reusable library
Users need to configure inputs, run operations, and inspect results

application_patterns.title: Service client
signals: The backend already runs independently
The GUI needs connection, loading, error, and retry states

application_patterns.title: File-oriented workbench
signals: Users open or create files and inspect or transform their contents
The interface needs navigation, editing, preview, and export

application_patterns.title: Multi-document command workbench
signals: Users continuously edit several peer documents or work surfaces
A dominant canvas is surrounded by project hierarchy, contextual commands, splits, and diagnostics

application_patterns.title: Spatial authoring workbench
signals: Users directly manipulate a scene, graph, canvas, or other spatial artifact
Hierarchy selection drives contextual tools, properties, and collapsible diagnostics

application_patterns.title: Nearby endpoint transfer flow
signals: Users discover nearby endpoints, choose a payload and destination, then observe transfer progress
The workflow is short, responsive, and must expose discovery, acceptance, failure, and completion clearly

application_patterns.title: Live production console
signals: A preview or program output remains active while users adjust sources and controls
Continuous meters, armed or active states, ordering, and immediate operator feedback must stay visible

application_patterns.title: Document knowledge workspace
signals: Users organize durable documents or records in a workspace hierarchy
One knowledge object can switch between text, grid, board, or other structured views

application_patterns.title: Command runner
signals: Users launch long-running operations and need progress, cancellation, and a designed result surface
A raw log widget is correct only when the product is itself a log viewer

application_patterns.title: Data dashboard
signals: Users monitor collections, status, and trends
Readability and refresh states matter more than document editing

application_patterns.title: Multi-page desktop application
signals: The product has several top-level work areas
Navigation, settings, persistence, and platform packaging are first-class requirements

application_patterns.title: Agent artifact workbench
signals: A prompt-driven agent creates or edits durable artifacts
Users need to inspect work products while run details remain secondary

application_patterns.title: Agent run workspace
signals: Users send a task and watch an ordered run of user, assistant, tool, and permission events
The transcript is the signature surface; a session list is supporting chrome, not a generic chat shell

application_patterns.title: Build pipeline workspace
signals: Work advances through ordered stages with observable progress
Users diagnose individual steps and retry or cancel a run

application_patterns.title: Artifact review workbench
signals: Users compare, annotate, or approve durable files or documents
Hierarchy and revision location matter more than a chronological chat

application_patterns.title: Event replay console
signals: The authoritative state is reconstructed from an ordered event stream
Users inspect sequence boundaries, decisions, recovery, and replay state

application_patterns.title: Multi-agent orchestrator
signals: Several autonomous workers own concurrent tasks or resources
Identity, coordination, exceptions, and handoffs must remain visible

selection_guides.question: How should a user invoke an action?

candidates.choose_when: One immediate action needs a standard, accent, or subtle push surface.
candidates.avoid_when: The action must remain active while pressed or expose secondary choices.

candidates.choose_when: An action needs a persistent secondary explanation below its primary label.
candidates.avoid_when: A concise label already communicates the action.

candidates.choose_when: Holding the pointer or key should invoke the same action repeatedly.
candidates.avoid_when: Repeated activation could duplicate a destructive or asynchronous operation.

candidates.choose_when: The action navigates to a URL and should read visually as a link.
candidates.avoid_when: The action changes local state without navigation.

candidates.choose_when: The surface only opens a menu of related commands.
candidates.avoid_when: The primary part must also invoke a default action.

candidates.choose_when: A primary action and a menu of alternatives share one surface.
candidates.avoid_when: There is no safe or obvious default action.

candidates.choose_when: The primary action toggles state while the secondary part exposes related options.
candidates.avoid_when: State and options are independent concepts that should use separate controls.

candidates.choose_when: Users choose or drop local files with clear validation feedback; the application owns browsing and file policy.
candidates.avoid_when: The surface must implement storage, upload transport, authentication, or queue persistence.

selection_guides.question: How should a user choose or adjust a value?

candidates.choose_when: An independent option may be on, off, or optionally indeterminate.
candidates.avoid_when: Exactly one item must be chosen from a visible set.

candidates.choose_when: Users need visual color selection with numeric or alpha editing.
candidates.avoid_when: Only a small fixed palette is allowed.

candidates.choose_when: One value is selected from a compact list that need not stay visible.
candidates.avoid_when: All alternatives must remain visible for comparison, or the control is pane chrome on window material.

candidates.choose_when: Several rows must be selected from a compact model-backed list, optionally with local search and filtered select all.
candidates.avoid_when: Users must author free-form tags, query a remote service, or compare every option at once.

candidates.choose_when: Exactly one option from a small visible group may be selected.
candidates.avoid_when: The option set is long, dynamic, or space constrained.

candidates.choose_when: Users view or set an ordered star-style rating.
candidates.avoid_when: The numeric value needs precise arbitrary input.

candidates.choose_when: A bounded numeric value benefits from direct relative adjustment.
candidates.avoid_when: Exact text entry is the primary requirement.

candidates.choose_when: A button-like command surface also communicates an on/off state.
candidates.avoid_when: The setting should read as a persistent form preference.

candidates.choose_when: A persistent binary setting takes effect immediately.
candidates.avoid_when: Submitting a form is required before the value takes effect.

candidates.choose_when: Users search and select one or several nodes from a hierarchy. Compose TreeView, Popup and native inputs; retain caller-owned models and stable keys.
candidates.avoid_when: Choices have no hierarchy; use ComboBox, MultiSelectComboBox or TagInput.

selection_guides.question: How should a collection or sequence be presented?

candidates.choose_when: Items form a primarily vertical collection, stream, conversation, event history, or log. Use a QAbstractItemModel and delegate so long or growing data stays virtualized; the built-in delegate covers ordinary text and icon rows, while richer rows use a bounded custom delegate.
candidates.avoid_when: Hierarchy or two-dimensional visual scanning is the main task, or the implementation would defeat virtualization with one persistent widget per row.

candidates.choose_when: Rows and columns need headers, aligned fields, sorting, multi-selection, or delegate-based cell editing over a QAbstractItemModel.
candidates.avoid_when: The content is a visual card gallery, a wrapping collection, or a parent-child hierarchy.

candidates.choose_when: Uniform visual items should be scanned in rows and columns.
candidates.avoid_when: Items vary substantially in size or form a hierarchy.

candidates.choose_when: Variable-sized items should wrap responsively like tags or cards.
candidates.avoid_when: Uniform cells or strict row alignment are required.

candidates.choose_when: The data has expandable parent-child hierarchy.
candidates.avoid_when: The hierarchy is only navigational and should use page navigation instead.

candidates.choose_when: Users browse one item or page at a time in a short sequence.
candidates.avoid_when: Users need to compare several items simultaneously.

candidates.choose_when: Pages follow push, pop, and back navigation semantics.
candidates.avoid_when: Peer pages need persistent visible tabs or top-level navigation.

candidates.choose_when: A caller-owned file model needs complete names, metadata, transfer progress, remove and retry actions.
candidates.avoid_when: Rows are general content unrelated to files or the view should own upload work.

candidates.choose_when: Ordered model rows need a timeline rail, supporting text and status.
candidates.avoid_when: The application needs a workflow navigation control instead of a record view.

selection_guides.question: How should dates and times be selected?

candidates.choose_when: A compact field should open a calendar for one optional date.
candidates.avoid_when: The calendar must stay visible.

candidates.choose_when: Users need a persistent month surface for browsing and date selection.
candidates.avoid_when: Screen space is constrained and selection is occasional.

candidates.choose_when: A compact locale-aware day, month, and year field is preferred over a calendar.
candidates.avoid_when: Users need surrounding-day context.

candidates.choose_when: Users select a locale-aware time of day.
candidates.avoid_when: The value represents duration rather than clock time.

candidates.choose_when: A compact query filter needs a calendar range popup, independently nullable start/end dates, minute precision, or whole-day presets.
candidates.avoid_when: The application needs one date, a duration, or non-contiguous date selection.

selection_guides.question: Which transient surface should present temporary content?

candidates.choose_when: A same-window modal decision needs a title, content, and up to three commit actions.
candidates.avoid_when: The task must remain modeless or needs a separate top-level window.

candidates.choose_when: Arbitrary modal content requires its own window surface.
candidates.avoid_when: A compact decision fits the same-window content-dialog contract.

candidates.choose_when: Contextual content should anchor to an invoking control and dismiss lightly.
candidates.avoid_when: The content must remain open while users work elsewhere.

candidates.choose_when: A low-level positioned overlay is needed and the application owns its complete behavior.
candidates.avoid_when: Flyout, menu, tooltip, or dialog already expresses the intended semantics.

candidates.choose_when: An anchored tip introduces a feature without blocking the rest of the application.
candidates.avoid_when: The message is routine status or validation feedback.

candidates.choose_when: A standalone guided tip must point at targets and move between them.
candidates.avoid_when: A simple anchored teaching tip is sufficient.

selection_guides.question: How should related content be grouped or revealed?

candidates.choose_when: Related content needs a token-backed rounded visual surface.
candidates.avoid_when: Grouping is already clear from hierarchy and spacing.

candidates.choose_when: Adjacent regions need a lightweight visual separator.
candidates.avoid_when: A separate Card or additional spacing communicates structure more clearly.

candidates.choose_when: An existing editor needs a shared label and validation feedback. Add FormController to coordinate dirty/touched state, asynchronous validation and submission while the application retains values and requests.
candidates.avoid_when: The editor already provides the complete labeling and validation presentation, or the content is not an editable field.

candidates.choose_when: One section independently reveals optional caller-owned content.
candidates.avoid_when: Several sections require coordinated expansion behavior.

candidates.choose_when: Several vertically stacked sections need coordinated single or multiple expansion.
candidates.avoid_when: Only one disclosure region exists.

candidates.choose_when: A temporary panel should slide over content from a window edge.
candidates.avoid_when: Both regions must remain visible and resizable.

candidates.choose_when: Two or more persistent regions need draggable size allocation.
candidates.avoid_when: The secondary region is temporary or modal.

candidates.choose_when: A bounded hero or panel needs CPU-painted ribbons, floating dots or a starfield behind normal child controls, with shared motion and density controls.
candidates.avoid_when: The animation communicates essential information or a large collection would create many continuously animating instances.

candidates.choose_when: A list and its detail should share the available width, collapsing to one persistent pane in a narrow space while keeping selection and editor state.
candidates.avoid_when: More than two panes, draggable splitting, docking, or overlay behavior is required.

candidates.choose_when: A DataGrid needs a wrapping search field, multi-select facets and column visibility, pinning or ordering controls. Connect its signals to an application-owned proxy model.
candidates.avoid_when: The view should own business filtering, loading or persistence, or no table is present.

candidates.choose_when: A bounded set of explicit typed properties needs generated Fluent editors, groups, search, reset and form validation. Applications own values and persistence.
candidates.avoid_when: An unbounded object tree, multi-object editing or a virtualized data table is required.

selection_guides.question: How should several commands be organized?

candidates.choose_when: A transient vertical list of commands is opened from context or a button.
candidates.avoid_when: Primary commands must remain visible.

candidates.choose_when: A desktop application needs persistent top-level command categories.
candidates.avoid_when: The application has only a few task-focused actions.

candidates.choose_when: Primary actions should stay visible while lower-priority commands overflow responsively.
candidates.avoid_when: Commands are purely contextual to one pointer location.

candidates.choose_when: A contextual surface combines primary and secondary command groups.
candidates.avoid_when: A simple menu or persistent command bar is sufficient.

candidates.choose_when: Users need keyboard search across grouped application commands with shared QAction state.
candidates.avoid_when: A short fixed menu already exposes every relevant command.

selection_guides.question: How should users move between application areas?

candidates.choose_when: Several top-level areas need adaptive application navigation and a content host.
candidates.avoid_when: Only a few peer views exist inside one local context.

candidates.choose_when: Users manage several open documents or peer work surfaces with visible tabs.
candidates.avoid_when: The destinations are fixed top-level product areas.

candidates.choose_when: A small set of peer views uses text headers and an animated indicator.
candidates.avoid_when: Users add, close, or reorder views.

candidates.choose_when: A compact row of selectable items switches among nearby views.
candidates.avoid_when: Deep hierarchy or overflow-heavy navigation is expected.

candidates.choose_when: Users need the current hierarchical path and direct navigation to ancestors.
candidates.avoid_when: The product structure is flat or the trail would duplicate top-level navigation.

candidates.choose_when: A small sequence needs current, completion and error states with application-controlled navigation requests.
candidates.avoid_when: The control must own validation, business actions or a large data collection.

selection_guides.question: How should content beyond the viewport be navigated?

candidates.choose_when: One caller-owned document, canvas, or deliberately finite widget composition needs a scrollable viewport with Fluent scrollbars and optional zoom.
candidates.avoid_when: A Qt item view already owns scrolling, or records can grow into an unbounded layout of child widgets.

candidates.choose_when: A custom scrolling host needs a standalone Fluent scrollbar.
candidates.avoid_when: ScrollView or an item view can own the complete viewport.

candidates.choose_when: Long content benefits from semantic labels or landmarks along its scroll range.
candidates.avoid_when: The content is short or labels would add noise.

candidates.choose_when: A short sequence needs dot-style page navigation.
candidates.avoid_when: The page count is large or exact page numbers matter.

selection_guides.question: How should status, progress, help, or identity be communicated?

candidates.choose_when: A person or identity needs an image, initials fallback, and optional presence.
candidates.avoid_when: The image is generic content rather than identity.

candidates.choose_when: A compact count, icon, or attention dot annotates another surface.
candidates.avoid_when: The message needs explanatory text or an action.

candidates.choose_when: Persistent inline status or validation feedback needs severity and optional actions.
candidates.avoid_when: The message is brief, nonessential, and can disappear automatically.

candidates.choose_when: Progress is naturally read along a horizontal range or in a content row.
candidates.avoid_when: Space is constrained to a compact square indicator.

candidates.choose_when: A compact circular indicator communicates determinate or indeterminate activity.
candidates.avoid_when: Users need precise progress comparison across a long operation.

candidates.choose_when: A startup surface must cover a host's content with artwork, title, status and progress. Branded is the default reveal; Simple retains the centered ring. An optional same-window transitionTarget connects dismissal to an application icon holder.
candidates.avoid_when: Content should remain interactive during background loading, or the component would need to own startup tasks.

candidates.choose_when: A skeleton placeholder should preserve content geometry while data loads.
candidates.avoid_when: The operation has explicit measurable progress or failed.

candidates.choose_when: A brief same-window notification confirms an outcome without interrupting work.
candidates.avoid_when: The user must acknowledge or resolve the condition.

candidates.choose_when: A concise hover or focus hint clarifies an otherwise understandable control.
candidates.avoid_when: Critical instructions or validation errors must remain visible.

selection_guides.question: How should text or numeric values be entered and displayed?

candidates.choose_when: Static text needs Fluent typography, wrapping, or elision.
candidates.avoid_when: The text must be edited.

candidates.choose_when: Read-only source needs syntax colors, exact copying, folding or bounded scrolling.
candidates.avoid_when: Users need to edit code or inspect a full file/project workspace.

candidates.choose_when: Users enter one line of general text.
candidates.avoid_when: Suggestions, numeric validation, passwords, or multiple lines are central.

candidates.choose_when: One-line input benefits from local or asynchronous suggestions. AutoSuggestBox owns debounce, request tokens, loading, empty, retry and pagination presentation; the application owns transport and borrowed model data.
candidates.avoid_when: The choice set is small and fixed enough for ComboBox.

candidates.choose_when: Users need validated numeric input with spin controls or expressions.
candidates.avoid_when: Relative dragging is more important than exact entry.

candidates.choose_when: Sensitive single-line input must be concealed with optional reveal behavior.
candidates.avoid_when: The value is not secret.

candidates.choose_when: Users enter or inspect multiple lines of text, logs, or documents.
candidates.avoid_when: Only a short single-line value is expected.

candidates.choose_when: Users choose several stable values as removable tags while searching. Reuses AutoSuggestBox; application-owned suggestion models and transport remain separate from selected value snapshots.
candidates.avoid_when: A fixed checklist-style dropdown is sufficient; use MultiSelectComboBox then.

selection_guides.question: Which primitives establish the application window and iconography?

candidates.choose_when: A top-level Fluent application window with custom chrome, Mica or Acrylic material, and theming is required.
candidates.avoid_when: The UI is embedded inside an existing host-owned window.

candidates.choose_when: A host window needs a reusable custom title bar and drag regions.
candidates.avoid_when: Fluent Window already owns the complete chrome contract.

candidates.choose_when: A theme-aware bundled Fluent glyph should render as a widget.
candidates.avoid_when: A product-specific illustration or arbitrary image is required.

selection_guides.question: How should indexed numerical data be plotted?

candidates.choose_when: A runtime-selectable chart host is needed. Prefer a dedicated chart component for a fixed presentation.
candidates.avoid_when: GPU density plots, stacked series, logarithmic axes, or financial charting are required. Build large ChartData snapshots off the GUI thread rather than resetting raw data every frame.

candidates.choose_when: Compare indexed time or XY series with bounded extrema-preserving projection.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not pass full histories per frame; prepare indexed ChartData snapshots off the GUI thread.

candidates.choose_when: Show trend magnitude with a restrained filled baseline.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not pass full histories per frame; prepare indexed ChartData snapshots off the GUI thread.

candidates.choose_when: Compare grouped categories; dense buckets expose their mean and source range.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not pass full histories per frame; prepare indexed ChartData snapshots off the GUI thread.

candidates.choose_when: Compare named categories horizontally; setYRange(0, 100) for percent data.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not pass full histories per frame; prepare indexed ChartData snapshots off the GUI thread.

candidates.choose_when: Compare a small set of positive contributions as a full disk.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not pass full histories per frame; prepare indexed ChartData snapshots off the GUI thread.

candidates.choose_when: Compare positive contributions with optional center text and a responsive legend.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not pass full histories per frame; prepare indexed ChartData snapshots off the GUI thread.

candidates.choose_when: Show representative XY samples; this is not a density estimator.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not pass full histories per frame; prepare indexed ChartData snapshots off the GUI thread.

candidates.choose_when: Embed a compact trend with no axes, card or metric ownership.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not pass full histories per frame; prepare indexed ChartData snapshots off the GUI thread.

selection_guides.question: How can a Widgets application reuse a QML page and business model?

candidates.choose_when: An existing QWidget window should embed a trusted QML page and share application-owned QObject or QAbstractItemModel data. Enable QmlBridge, bind context objects before load, and use fluentTheme tokens explicitly.
candidates.avoid_when: The application needs automatic QWidget-to-Quick conversion, untrusted script isolation, or a new Qt Quick control library. Coordinate the graphics API before mixing Quick and Spatial in one window.

selection_guides.question: How can existing widgets gain perspective and depth?

candidates.choose_when: A small C++ showcase or preview should host real Fluent widgets with perspective and pointer tilt. Compose ordinary Cards first and provide a 2D mode.
candidates.avoid_when: The task needs mesh rendering, many live surfaces, native child windows, or primary text editing and popups in perspective.

candidates.choose_when: A widget already added to SpatialView needs an independent position, rotation, scale or pivot. Use the handle returned by addWidget().
candidates.avoid_when: A normal layout, a standalone widget, or automatic extraction of a widget paint layer is required.

import QtQuick 2.15

Rectangle {
    color: fluentTheme.surface
    radius: fluentTheme.cornerRadius
    antialiasing: true
    property string previewTitle: widgetInput ? widgetInput.text : ""

    Rectangle {
        anchors.fill: parent
        z: -1
        color: fluentTheme.surfaceAlt
    }

    Text {
        anchors.centerIn: parent
        width: parent.width - 32
        horizontalAlignment: Text.AlignHCenter
        text: parent.previewTitle
        elide: Text.ElideRight
        color: fluentTheme.text
        font.family: fluentTheme.fontFamily
        font.pixelSize: fluentTheme.fontPixelSize
    }
}
